description: Four-panel composite of electron-microscopy deformation and fracture data for the long annealed (650 °C/72 h) 2Al steel; all four panels are grayscale electron images (no plots, no axes). (a) Electron channelling contrast imaging (ECCI) of the grain interior at 500 nm scale bar: a mottled dark-light substructure of roughly equiaxed dislocation cell blocks, with a bright rounded spot at upper left and a smoother featureless band at lower right. (b) Lower-magnification ECCI, 10 µm scale bar: dark equiaxed grains outlined by bright grain-boundary networks, with discrete bright particles decorating the boundaries and straight annealing-twin traces. (c) ECCI, 1 µm scale bar: parallel straight deformation-twin bands crossing a grain, intercepted by a diagonal chain of bright blocky intergranular carbides. (d) SEM fracture surface, 10 µm scale bar: faceted, equiaxed grain-shaped faces with sharp edges and intergranular cracking. The panels together argue that twin bands impinging on coarse intergranular M3C carbides concentrate shear stress at carbide interfaces and trigger intergranular fracture. Only panel letters and scale bars are printed; no numeric data appear in the pixels.

subfigures.description: ECCI micrograph of the deformed grain interior with a 500 nm scale bar: a mottled dark-light network of roughly equiaxed dislocation cell blocks, plus a bright rounded spot at upper left and a smoother band at lower right.

ECCI micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar: several dark equiaxed grains separated by bright grain boundaries that are decorated with discrete bright particles; faint straight twin boundary traces visible inside grains.

ECCI micrograph with a 1 µm scale bar: closely spaced parallel straight deformation-twin bands crossing the field, intercepted by a diagonal chain of bright blocky intergranular carbide particles, with dark blobs at lower left.
SEM fracture surface with a 10 µm scale bar: faceted, grain-shaped three-dimensional faces with sharp ridges and deep intergranular cracks, characteristic of an intergranular fracture mode.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an electron channelling contrast (ECCI) micrograph whose contrast is dominated by a mottled network of roughly equiaxed dislocation cell blocks in the grain interior.
Panel (a) carries a 500 nm scale bar in its lower-left corner; no other numeric annotation is present in the panel.
Panel (b) carries a 10 µm scale bar and shows dark equiaxed grains separated by bright grain-boundary networks decorated with discrete bright particles.
Panel (c) carries a 1 µm scale bar and shows closely spaced parallel straight bands (deformation twins) intersected by a diagonal chain of bright blocky particles along a boundary.
Panel (d) carries a 10 µm scale bar and shows a faceted fracture surface made of grain-shaped faces with sharp edges and open intergranular cracks.

The caption identifies (a) as ECCI of dislocation cell blocks in a sample strained to 0.2 true strain and (c) as ECCI of deformation twin-intergranular M3C-type carbide interactions in a sample strained to fracture.
The caption states that (b) shows the distribution of intergranular M3C-type carbides and (d) shows a surface fracture revealing an intergranular fracture mode.

The citing text states the dislocation cell block size at 0.2 true strain in the long annealed 2Al steel is 275 ± 50 nm, comparable to 270 ± 70 nm for the short annealed 2Al steel at 950 MPa true stress.
The citing text states the intergranular carbides are about 1 µm wide by 3 µm long and correspond to incoherent M3C-type carbides; these dimensions are not measurable from the printed pixels alone.
The citing text gives an estimated twinning stress σ_twinning ~ 670-750 MPa (γ = 60 mJ m^-2, b = 0.25 nm, Taylor factor 2.8-3.2) associated with the twin bundles seen in (c).

The citing text states the long annealed sample fractures at a macroscopic true stress of 1150 MPa with limited elongation (UE = 35%), linked to twin-intergranular carbide damage rather than additional hardening.
The intergranular fracture surface in (d) is consistent with the caption/citation claim that twin-tip impingement on coarse intergranular M3C carbides concentrates shear stress at carbide interfaces.

unreadable_items: panel (a): the bright rounded spot at upper left is of unclear origin (possible imaging artifact) and cannot be identified from the pixels
carbide dimensions in (b) and (c) cannot be measured from the pixels; only the caption/citation values are available
number of deformation twins per bundle in (c) cannot be counted reliably from the supplied resolution
